task:
Add shop/cache.py with class TtlCache(ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic),
built on the LRU class in shop/lru.py. Methods: set(key, value), get(key, default=None), delete(key) -> bool,
"key in cache" and len(cache). An entry expires once clock() - stored_at >= ttl_seconds, so it is already gone
exactly at the ttl. set() on an existing key replaces the value and restarts its ttl; get() does not extend the
ttl. len() and "in" count only live entries. When max_size is set and a new key is inserted into a full cache,
expired entries are dropped first and only if it is still full is the least recently used live entry evicted;
both get() hits and set() count as use. Updating an existing key never evicts anything. A stored value of None
is a real value. delete() returns True only if a live entry was removed. The cache must be safe to use from many
threads, and instances must not share any state (no module-level mutable state). Add unit tests.

units.title: Add LRU class in shop/lru.py with unit tests
units.spec:
shop/lru.py is not in the repository, so create it. Add `class LRU` backed by `collections.OrderedDict`. It is a plain recency-ordered map: it has no capacity, does no automatic eviction and has no locking. Create the OrderedDict in `__init__` as `self._data`.

API:
- `put(key, value) -> None`: insert or replace the value and mark the key most recently used (`move_to_end`).
- `get(key, default=None)`: if the key is present, mark it most recently used and return its value. Otherwise return `default`.
- `peek(key, default=None)`: like `get`, but does not change the order.
- `remove(key) -> bool`: delete the key. Return True if it was present, otherwise False.
- `pop_lru() -> tuple`: remove and return `(key, value)` for the least recently used entry. Raise `KeyError` if empty.
- `keys() -> list`: a snapshot list of keys, least recent first.
- `__len__` and `__contains__`. `__contains__` does not change the order.

A stored value of None is a normal value. Add a short module docstring and method docstrings.

Tests go in tests/test_lru.py using unittest, in the same style as the existing tests. Cover:
- put/get round-trip
- get of a missing key returns the default
- get moves the key to most recent, checked via `keys()` and `pop_lru`
- peek does not reorder
- put on an existing key replaces the value and moves it to most recent
- remove returns True/False correctly
- pop_lru on an empty LRU raises KeyError
- None is stored and returned
- two instances do not share state
acceptance: tests/test_lru.py covers get reordering, peek not reordering, pop_lru order and KeyError on empty
shop/lru.py has no module-level mutable state

units.title: Add TtlCache in shop/cache.py built on LRU, with unit tests
units.spec:
Create shop/cache.py with `class TtlCache` and constructor `__init__(self, ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic)`. Raise ValueError if `max_size` is not None and `max_size < 1`.

Per-instance state:
- `self._ttl`
- `self._max_size`
- `self._clock`
- `self._lru = LRU()` (from shop.lru)
- `self._lock = threading.RLock()`

Use a private module-level immutable sentinel, `_MISSING = object()`, so that a stored None can be told apart from a missing key.

The LRU stores `(value, stored_at)` tuples. Define `_expired(stored_at, now)` as `now - stored_at >= self._ttl`, so an entry is already gone exactly at the ttl.

Every public method takes the lock for its whole body and calls `self._clock()` once.

- `set(key, value)`:
  - If the key exists in the LRU (live or expired), `put` it with `(value, now)`. This replaces the value, restarts the ttl and marks it as used. An update never evicts.
  - Otherwise, if `max_size` is set and `len(self._lru) >= max_size`, first drop all expired entries using a private `_purge(now)`. `_purge` iterates `self._lru.keys()`, uses `peek` and calls `remove` on expired entries. If the LRU is still at least `max_size` long, call `pop_lru()` once. Then `put` the new entry.
- `get(key, default=None)`:
  - Look the key up with `peek`. If it is missing, return `default`.
  - If it is expired, `remove` it and return `default`.
  - Otherwise call `self._lru.get(key)` to mark it as used and return the value.
  - Do NOT change `stored_at`.
- `delete(key) -> bool`: use `peek`. If the key is missing, return False. If it is expired, remove it and return False. If it is live, remove it and return True.
- `__contains__(key)`: return True only for a live entry. Do not change recency. Removing the entry if it has expired is fine.
- `__len__()`: call `_purge(now)`, then return `len(self._lru)`.

Tests go in tests/test_cache.py using unittest. Use a fake clock object with a mutable `t` attribute and `__call__` returning `t`, and advance time manually. Cover:
- set/get
- missing key returns the default
- entry live at ttl-epsilon and gone exactly at ttl (get, `in` and len all agree)
- set on an existing key restarts the ttl
- get does not extend the ttl
- len and `in` ignore expired entries
- None is a real value (`get(k, 'd')` returns None and `k in cache` is True)
- delete returns True for a live entry, and False for an expired or missing one
- eviction with max_size=2:
  - Insert a, b. Get a. Insert c. Then b is evicted and a and c remain.
  - set also counts as use: insert a, b, set a again, insert c, and b is evicted.
- expired entries are dropped before evicting a live one: with max_size=2, insert a, advance time so a expires, insert b, insert c, and b and c both remain
- updating an existing key in a full cache evicts nothing
- ValueError for max_size=0
- two instances are independent
- a thread-safety test: 8 threads each doing about 1000 mixed set/get/delete calls on a shared cache with max_size=50. Assert there are no exceptions and that `len(cache) <= 50`.

Also add a `- cache.py — TTL cache with optional LRU size limit` bullet and an `lru.py` bullet to the README code list.
acceptance: An entry is absent from get/in/len exactly when clock() - stored_at == ttl_seconds
LRU eviction respects get hits and set as use; expired entries are purged before any live eviction
Updating an existing key in a full cache leaves all other keys present
Concurrency test with 8 threads completes without exceptions

rules.text: Standard library only; use unittest for tests, run via `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
No module-level mutable state; the only module-level object allowed in cache.py is the immutable _MISSING sentinel. Each instance owns its own LRU and lock.
Time comes only from the injected clock (default time.monotonic); never call time.time/sleep in cache logic, and tests use a fake clock rather than sleeping.
All TtlCache public methods hold the instance lock for their entire body; LRU itself stays lock-free.
Keep functions small and add docstrings, matching the existing shop/ style.

dont_list: Don't use `>` for expiry; expiry uses `>=` so an entry is gone exactly at the ttl.
Don't refresh stored_at on get(), and don't use self._lru.get() for lookups in __contains__ or for expired entries.
Don't use None as the 'not found' marker; None is a valid stored value.
Don't evict or purge when set() updates an existing key.
Don't evict the LRU entry before purging expired ones.
Don't use functools.lru_cache or a class-level/shared dict or lock.
Don't modify existing modules (cart, pricing, money, storage) or their tests.
